See docs/storybook-decisions.md.

scripts.//typecheck:all:nuxt: RESIDUAL-01, closing D-S2O1-1. packages/nuxt is a PUBLISHED package and appeared in neither `typecheck` nor `typecheck:all`, so it had no type gate at all -- which is how 17 errors (16 x TS6059 plus a narrowed union) sat in it until a red `yarn build` surfaced them, two days before this was wired. The project named here is the TYPECHECK view (no rootDir, no emit, contracts resolved from source); the BUILD view is tsconfig.build.json and is covered by the `yarn build` link at the end of validate:all. Both halves are needed: a --noEmit check cannot see the rootDir/emit contradiction that actually broke the package, and a build cannot see an error in a spec file it excludes.
scripts.//lint: packages/ AND both apps (TASK-FREE2-01). --max-warnings 0: the baseline is zero errors and zero warnings, so a new warning fails CI rather than accreting into a 'known baseline' everyone ignores. Generated output is excluded via eslint.config.js `ignores`, not CLI globs.

scripts.//regenerate:all: RESIDUAL-09, closing D-RES07-2 option (c). The SANCTIONED REGENERATION ORDER, executable: generate:ownership -> generate:quality-matrix -> generate:capability-matrix -> generate:component-meta -> generate:llms -> generate:docs-pages -> csp:inline-style-inventory. Seven steps, not six: step 7 appeared in NO documented order, is checked by NONE of validate:all's 61 links, and fails only in the unit suite (packages/core/security/inline-style-inventory.spec.ts), which is how two consecutive batches handed over a red suite. Why a script: the order was prose only, RESIDUAL-07 found it in six live locations and corrected all six, found a seventh already drifted to four commands, and its omissions broke three agents' validation runs in one programme. A list that must be hand-copied has proved it drifts; a script cannot. It REFUSES two things. (1) A step naming a script the root manifest does not declare -- checked BEFORE anything runs, because validator and script names diverge here (validate:ownership runs validators/ownership-manifest.ts) and a chain that discovers a rename at step 5 has already rewritten four artifacts. (2) Continuing past a failure -- it exits with the failing step's own code, names the step and its position, and LISTS THE STEPS THAT DID NOT RUN, because those are the artifacts a reader would otherwise assume are fresh. The annotated table in CLAUDE.md is deliberately KEPT and is bound to this order by a spec (packages/tooling/src/regenerate-all.spec.ts asserts the table and the script agree step for step): the table explains WHY each step is owed, which is the judgement a human makes when only one artifact is stale; the script guarantees WHAT runs when several are. `yarn regenerate:all --list` prints the order and each trigger without running anything.
scripts.//generate:tokens:dtcg: TASK-N2-T1. Emits packages/tokens/dist/tokens.dtcg.json -- the DTCG 2025.10 interchange projection of the same token maps `tokens:generate` turns into tokens.css. Deliberately a separate script from the tokens package `generate` (generate.ts also rewrites the repo-root DESIGN.md). Since 2026-09-24 the root `tokens:generate` runs it as a second step: `./dtcg` is in the tokens `exports` map, so merged-source resolution (every landing Vite config: build:counts, build:registry, ...) refuses to load on a clean checkout until the artifact exists. It writes only the git-ignored dist/tokens.dtcg.json. Output is deterministic and timestamp-free -- run it twice and diff. `yarn validate:tokens:dtcg` proves the file on disk is fresh AND that every token in it resolves to the value tokens.css ships.
scripts.//generate:ownership: TASK-OSS-P0-01. Regenerates packages/core/manifests/component-ownership.manifest.json -- the single deterministic answer to "who owns DzFoo?" that the resolver, the Nuxt module, and the cross-tier ownership map consume. It REPORTS: symbols no authority can classify are emitted as `unclassified` with their evidence, never guessed from a Dz prefix. Core has one tier, so :core is an alias kept for symmetry with Pro.
scripts.//generate:ownership:map: TASK-OSS-P0-02. Merges a Core and a Pro ownership manifest into one exact-name lookup. The Pro input is a FILE produced by a Pro checkout (Pro TASK-GOV-01) -- Core never reads Pro source. Exits non-zero on any cross-tier name collision: a collision is resolved only by a checked-in decision in packages/tooling/src/ownership/collision-decisions.json that names an ADR. Example: yarn generate:ownership:map -- --core packages/core/manifests/component-ownership.manifest.json --pro ../dzup-ui-pro/packages/pro/manifests/component-ownership.manifest.json --out /tmp/ownership-map.json
scripts.//generate:readme-facts: TASK-OSS-P2-02. Rewrites the marked fact regions of README.md from package.json and the ownership manifest. The package table was hand-typed and five of its six rows named a version the package had already moved past, while two publishable packages were missing entirely. Complements apps/landing build-counts.ts, which owns the separate claims:generated region of the same file.
scripts.//generate:mcp-surface: TASK-N2-A1. Rewrites packages/mcp/docs/mcp-tool-surface.json and the generated tool table in packages/mcp/README.md from a REAL MCP tools/list round-trip against the server the package ships, plus an observed data-source probe per tool (each tool is called through a reader that records the site paths it requests). The tool list previously existed in four hand-typed copies -- the source, the README, the smoke script and the CHANGELOG -- and nothing compared them. Deterministic: it probes committed fixtures, never apps/storybook/public/llms.txt, which is a git-ignored build output.
scripts.//generate:component-meta: TASK-N2-A2. The ONE extraction pipeline. Runs vue-component-meta over every component the ownership manifest classifies public-component or compound-part (208), reading the real .vue/.types.ts through a real TypeScript program, and joins the result to the capability matrix (family/tier/anatomy/evidence state) and to the stories files (verbatim example source) into packages/core/docs/component-meta.json. The docs site (N2-D1), llms-full.txt (N2-A3) and the three metadata MCP tools all read that file; none of them parses a .vue on its own. Drives its component list from the OWNERSHIP manifest, not public-api.manifest.json, which TASK-N2-A1 measured stale by 43 symbols. Deterministic: sorted throughout, printed with LF, absolute paths normalised; two cold runs are byte-identical.
scripts.//generate:llms: TASK-N2-A3. Renders packages/core/docs/llms.txt and llms-full.txt -- the files coding agents read, and the files @dzup-ui/mcp's list_components / get_component answer from -- entirely from packages/core/docs/component-meta.json plus the curated intro prose in packages/tooling/src/llms/llms-content.ts. It replaces apps/storybook/scripts/build-llms.mjs, which was a 567-line SECOND component-API extractor driven by public-api.manifest.json (stale by 43 public components, TASK-N2-A1 finding F1), so those 43 were invisible to every MCP client. apps/storybook's build:llms now only copies the committed output into the served public/ dir. Pure projection: no filesystem walk, no TypeScript program, no .vue parsed.
scripts.//generate:docs-pages: TASK-N2-D1. Writes apps/docs/components/<Name>.md (one per public component), apps/docs/components/index.md and apps/docs/.vitepress/generated/nav.json from packages/core/docs/component-meta.json. The page body is renderComponentSection() -- the SAME function llms-full.txt is rendered by, called with a page-level heading -- so the docs site and the agent documents cannot say different things and there is no second extractor (constraint B9). BEFORE writing anything it re-extracts every component from source and fails if the committed artifact disagrees, reusing validate:component-meta's own freshness clause: apps/docs's build script is `yarn generate && vitepress build`, so a stale artifact turns the SITE build red. Compound parts get no page of their own; all 64 are rendered inside their parent's page. --skip-freshness is a local-loop escape hatch that prints a banner and is refused by --check. TASK-N2-D2 added the evidence layer: an Accessibility-and-evidence section on every component page and six generated pages under apps/docs/evidence/, rendered from quality-matrix.json, capability-matrix.json, e2e/at-matrix/index.json, wcag-deviations.json and the two optional lane records (engine-ratchets.json, security-deviations.json), whose ABSENCE is printed on the page rather than routed around. Three further gates run BEFORE anything is written and refuse rather than report: the at-manual tripwire (a summary cell may not claim more than the append-only AT run records support -- N1-O4 section 6.2 measured that a component whose every pair FAILED resolves to pass, because CellState has no fail value), the capability cross-check (component-meta.json's capability join must agree with the capability matrix it was joined from) and the SC 2.5.7 audit binding (wcag-deviations.json must cover exactly the components the generated drags trait names).
scripts.//validate:hardcoded-strings: TASK-OSS-P4-03. Fails on a user-visible string a component hard-codes: a static aria-label in a template (nobody can change it -- there were 54), or a literal default on a *Text/*Label/*Placeholder prop (only changeable one instance at a time -- there were 39). Reads the <template> block only, so JSDoc @example strings are not swept up. Mark a line `hardcoded-string-ok: <reason>` when the value genuinely is not language; the reason lives at the string, not in a list.
scripts.//validate:i18n-packs: TASK-R5-O4 (N5-04 D4/F11). Every locale pack in packages/core/src/i18n/locales/*.json has every catalog key translated OR listed in its explicit `fallback` -- never silently missing -- and every translation parses and reads the same arguments as English. Also: en.json is byte-identical to enMessages, a pack's declared direction agrees with directionForLocale(), no source module imports a pack (tree-shaking), and the generated pseudo-locale formats. `as const satisfies DzMessageCatalog` cannot do any of this: it compares English to itself, and a pack is data. Runs in milliseconds, no browser.
scripts.//generate:i18n-packs: TASK-R5-O4. Rewrites en.json from enMessages and adds any key the catalog gained to each pack's `fallback` list (never translates, never deletes a translation). `tsx packages/tooling/src/validators/i18n-packs.ts --scaffold <locale>` starts a new pack with every key an explicit fallback; see packages/core/docs/i18n.md.
scripts.//validate:i18n-completeness: TASK-S5-O1. The PRODUCT question `validate:i18n-packs` does not ask. That gate proves a pack is structurally valid and every key accounted for -- and it exits 0 for a pack that copied English into every value, and for a 0 % scaffold that a release note then calls a supported locale. This one prints a per-locale COMPLETENESS PERCENTAGE with English-identical values subtracted, fails when an incomplete locale is not named in i18n-completeness-ceilings.json with the decision that made it incomplete (`undeclared-scaffold`), fails when the count of locales at >= 95 % falls below the floor (`supported-floor`, may only rise), and -- the check nothing else can make -- fails when a translated plural omits a category the LOCALE requires, read from Intl.PluralRules rather than a table: a Polish pack with only one/other parses, satisfies i18n-packs rule 4 and silently renders `other` for few and many. Also reports, never failing, which scripts have a typeface: AR-2's zero vendored fonts, re-measured each run (D63).
scripts.//i18n:new: TASK-S5-O1. `yarn i18n:new <bcp47-tag>` -- the documented first step of packages/core/docs/i18n.md section 5. Writes packages/core/src/i18n/locales/<tag>.json with every catalog key an explicit `fallback`, nothing translated, direction resolved by directionForLocale(); refuses to overwrite an existing pack. A LANE over the existing implementation (`i18n-packs.ts --scaffold`), not a second one -- the capability shipped in TASK-R5-O4 under a name a contributor reading the i18n docs would never guess.
scripts.//i18n:check: TASK-S5-O1. The one command a translator runs: both locale gates, structure then completeness, in the order their failures make sense in. Named `i18n:` rather than `validate:` because a contributor is not running the repository's validation suite, they are asking `is my pack finished yet` -- and the answer is a percentage.
scripts.//validate:security-corpus: TASK-R3-O4. The security-fixture format @dzup-ui/testing publishes for both repositories exists three ways -- TypeScript types, checkCorpusFile(), and the JSON Schemas shipped beside the data -- and this gate reads all three together: every schema enum equals the exported constant it mirrors, every JSON file in packages/testing/security-corpus is a known category file / the peer-compatibility file / a schema, every data file validates against its JSON Schema (json-schema-draft07.ts, no new dependency) AND the checker at the current schemaVersion, and the schema never rejects what the checker accepts. The peer-compatibility records are executed: bound to the dependent's real peerDependencies, and each validate-stage diagnostic must be what validate:peers actually prints. Before it, the only reader was a spec over the data, and there was no schema a second repository could validate against.
scripts.//validate:tv-slots: TASK-N2-S1, closes N1-O3 finding G1. A tv({ slots }) recipe returns FUNCTIONS; binding one without calling it (`:class="styles.closeButton"`) is valid TypeScript, valid Vue, and renders the element with NO classes at all -- Vue's normalizeClass has no branch for a function. DzLightbox shipped TEN of them and typecheck, lint, unit specs, contract specs and story-DoD all passed. This resolves every slot-bearing recipe in scope for each SFC (sibling and relatively-imported *.variants.ts, plus inline tv()), finds the identifiers they are bound to, and fails on any `binder.slot` / `binder.value.slot` not followed by a call, plus any destructured slot function used as a class value. A slot genuinely wanted as a value says `tv-slot-ok: <reason>` on the line.
scripts.//validate:anatomy-parts: TASK-N2-S1, ADR-19 validation-hook table row 2. Source-level alignment between the `data-part` attributes components EMIT and the anatomies that DECLARE them -- the hook ADR-19 assigns to `validate:contract-parity` and which was never built there, so until now nothing in the repository could see an emitted part with no governing declaration. Every static `data-part="x"` in packages/core/src must be declared by the component's own Dz{Name}.anatomy.ts or by the anatomy of a component that composes it (a compound part such as DzTableRow is covered by DzTable's declaration); every declared non-optional part must be emitted by some source. Reports part names outside the ADR-19 shared vocabulary rather than failing on them, which is what lets the vocabulary grow deliberately.
scripts.//validate:vendor-sublayers: TASK-R5-O1, ADR-19 s2/s3. The CSS half of the rule that keeps a dependency out of the public contract. ADR-19 s3 already says a Reka internal never becomes a `data-part`; nothing said the same about a `[data-reka-*]` SELECTOR inside @layer dz-components, which is the same bet on somebody else DOM with none of the visibility. packages/core/src/styles/vendor-registry.json is the ledger -- selector, owner, reason, exit condition -- and this gate enforces three things: an entry is complete, an entry is still live (its selector still exists in the CSS), and every vendor-shaped selector in the CSS has an entry. The registry is EMPTY, measured empty on 99b963a, which is exactly why the third rule matters: it is what stops the first one arriving unnoticed.
scripts.//test:e2e:layer-order: TASK-R5-O1, ADR-19 s2. The CSS layer / import-order fixture, on the PACKED TARBALLS rather than on source: yarn-packs @dzup-ui/tokens and @dzup-ui/core, reads dist/tokens.css and dist/core.css out of the .tgz, and asserts in chromium, firefox and webkit that all six ADR-19 layers are registered, that unlayered consumer CSS beats every library layer in BOTH import orders with no !important, that a consumer rule in @layer dz-overrides beats dz-components, and that a consumer sheet which registers dz-overrides BEFORE the library loses -- a measured CSS limit, asserted so it cannot change silently. Needs `yarn workspace @dzup-ui/tokens build` and `yarn workspace @dzup-ui/core build` first; it deliberately does NOT fall back to reading source. Playwright, so not part of validate:all.
scripts.//test:e2e:csp: TASK-R2-O4, closing TASK-N1-O5 owner decision O5-5. The strict-CSP lane: one Vite-built fixture mounting DzProvider + DzThemeProvider + DzFileUpload + two DzButtons, served TWICE from one Node server -- /open/ with no policy and /strict/ under a real Content-Security-Policy header with a per-request nonce and NO unsafe-inline anywhere. The assertion is equality between the two runs, because a lane that only looked at the strict run would pass on a page broken in both. jsdom does not enforce CSP at all, which is why the existing csp-fixture spec could only prove what the component EMITS. The fixture also carries a control element whose style attribute is in the served markup, so a green run cannot mean the header never arrived. Playwright, so not part of validate:all. The first run builds the fixture with Vite; later runs reuse the stage in the OS temp directory (DZUP_CSP_REBUILD=1 forces a rebuild).
scripts.//csp:inline-style-inventory: TASK-R2-O4. Re-derives packages/core/security/inline-style-inventory.json -- every style attribute and :style binding in the published component source, with a disposition per site. TASK-N1-O5 finding F-C1 measured 78 and 38 and stopped; this is the classification that makes acting on them reviewable. packages/core/security/inline-style-inventory.spec.ts fails when the artifact and the source disagree and when any count rises. RUN THIS AFTER ANY EDIT TO A .vue THAT CARRIES AN INLINE style= -- the artifact records the LINE NUMBER of every site, so a one-line insertion makes it stale even when nothing was added or removed. No link of the sanctioned regeneration order (ownership -> quality -> capability -> component-meta -> llms -> docs-pages) refreshes it and validate:all does not check it at all, so the only gate that fails is the unit suite. Measured RESIDUAL-07 (2026-09-25): the six links ran end to end, all exit 0, and the artifact was still stale afterwards.
scripts.//generate:rtl-matrix: TASK-OSS-P4-05. Rewrites packages/core/docs/rtl-matrix.md from the `rtl` field each component declares in its anatomy, so the table cannot drift from the declarations the way a hand-maintained one does.
scripts.//validate:rtl: TASK-OSS-P4-05. A component that declares `rtl: { mirrors: 'layout' }` must not use physical left/right utilities in its variants -- and the generated matrix must match the declarations. A deliberate physical case says `rtl-physical-ok` in the file with its reason (code blocks, `align="left"`, a sheet side the author named). Source-level only: whether `margin-inline-start` resolves to the correct physical edge needs an engine that does layout, which is `expectRtlComputed` in the Playwright lane.
scripts.//generate:form-readiness: TASK-FORM-OSS-01. Rewrites docs/program-2026-08/form-controls-readiness-matrix.md from the ownership manifest (which controls exist), a source probe (what they do), the quality matrix (their APG pattern) and the reviewed assessments in packages/tooling/src/forms/assessments.ts. Nothing in the table is typed by hand, so TASK-FORM-OSS-02 flips a cell by fixing the component and re-running this -- not by editing the row.
scripts.//validate:form-readiness: TASK-FORM-OSS-01. Fails when the committed readiness matrix is stale, when a form control has no assessment or an assessment names a control that no longer exists, and when a reviewed pass carries no evidence. Where a clause is decidable from source -- C2 identity, C3 states, C5 SSR, C6, C7, C8 -- the probe is final and a review cannot upgrade it.
scripts.//generate:quality-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-01. Joins the ownership manifest, the tier rules in @dzup-ui/contracts, and the reviewed assignment in packages/tooling/src/quality/component-tiers.ts into packages/core/docs/quality-matrix.json -- the single answer to "what evidence does DzX owe", which every other P5 packet reads instead of re-deriving it.
scripts.//validate:quality-tiers: TASK-OSS-P5-01. The tier assignment is the one handwritten inventory here, so it is the one most able to drift: this fails when a public component has no tier, when a tier is assigned to a symbol that stopped being public, when a Tier C/D or `custom` pattern carries no reason, when a WCAG id or an exception names something outside the catalog, when a component renders teleported content without declaring the trait, when a component's own anatomy contradicts the assignment, or when the generated matrix is stale.
scripts.//generate:matrix-targets: TASK-OSS-P5-03. Rewrites e2e/matrix/targets.generated.ts from quality-matrix.json and the story corpus, so the browser matrix covers every Tier B-D component the moment it becomes public. A component with no story is emitted with `story: null` and reported as unrun, never dropped.
scripts.//generate:browser-evidence: TASK-R2-O1. Projects Playwright JSON reports from the browser matrix into e2e/matrix/browser-evidence.json -- the TRACKED per-{component, engine, condition} record the capability matrix reads. It replaces test-results/matrix-report.json, which is git-ignored (N0-05 F4) AND lives inside the directory Playwright empties at the start of every run, so the 2026-08-25 record N1-O2 decision D1 set out to protect no longer exists. Write reports OUTSIDE test-results/ (PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT) and pass each with --report; projects no report covers keep the cells and the run provenance they already had, or stay `unrun` with a reason. Nothing is ever copied here from a prose ledger. `--probe-engines <out.json>` launches the three engines once to record their versions; `--reset` starts the ledger from nothing. Example: yarn generate:browser-evidence --report ../reports/matrix-chromium.json --engine-versions ../reports/engines.json
scripts.//generate:at-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-04. Writes one e2e/at-matrix/{Component}.md per Tier B-D component and the index.json the capability matrix reads. The generator owns everything ABOVE the results marker and never rewrites a recorded run below it.
scripts.//validate:at-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-04. Fails on a malformed or unevidenced row -- an unknown AT pair, an unrecognised result, a `pass` with no versions/tester/date/commit behind it, or an index that disagrees with the markdown. Unrun and stale cells are REPORTED, not failed: every row in a new matrix starts unrun, and a gate that failed on that would be switched off the day it landed.
scripts.//generate:at-scripts: TASK-N1-O4. Writes e2e/at-matrix/scripts/{Component}.at-script.md for the 22 Tier C/D components -- the story to open, the keys to press and the announcement the AT must produce, one step per scaffold task. It writes instructions only: no result is read or written here, and nothing under the scaffold's append-only marker is touched.
scripts.//validate:at-scripts: TASK-N1-O4. Script QA, not a test result. Fails when a Tier C/D component has no script, when a scaffold task has no step (or two), when a step invents a task the pattern does not imply, when a step sends a tester to a story id the built Storybook does not have, or when the files on disk have drifted from the data. WIRED INTO validate:all by TASK-R2-O2 (N1-O4 owner decision #10), immediately before validate:at-matrix: the scripts are what a human is sent to execute, and a drifted script sends a tester to a story that no longer exists or asks for a task the pattern no longer implies -- a failure mode whose cost is measured in tester-hours, not CI minutes, and which the scaffold gate beside it cannot see. It runs BEFORE validate:at-matrix because a script that does not resolve makes the matrix's cells unexecutable in the first place.
scripts.//at:ingest: TASK-S1-O1. Ingests ONE human tester's AT session record (JSON) into the matrix: validates it, appends one eight-column row per step beneath the append-only marker, archives the full record under e2e/at-matrix/runs/ and rebuilds index.json. It TRANSCRIBES a result a named person produced -- it never generates one, and an agent never runs it against a record an agent wrote. FAILS CLOSED and whole: a record missing the tester, the AT or browser version, the OS, the sourceCommit, a date that is not a real past day, a task the component does not owe, a verdict stronger than its steps, or a duplicate of a session already recorded is refused entirely and NOTHING is written. Record format: docs/qa/at-run-record.md. Flags: --dry-run, --matrix-dir <dir> (a scratch copy; the only place --allow-fixture is permitted).
scripts.//validate:at-runs: TASK-S1-O1. Cross-checks the archived session records under e2e/at-matrix/runs/ against the matrix rows they produced. Catches the three ways manual evidence stops being evidence: an archive whose rows never reached the matrix (an interrupted ingest -- somebody's 21 hours in a directory nothing reads), a row hand-edited after ingest (the one with teeth: the resolver would publish the edit and the archive contradicting it would sit beside it silently), and a JSON dropped into runs/ by hand, bypassing at:ingest and its refusals. Chained at the END of validate:all so every existing link number holds. It exits 0 over an empty directory today -- 534 cells, 0 executed -- and becomes load-bearing the day wave 1 is ingested; it is deliberately built before the evidence, because the first tester's records are the ones most likely to be mishandled.
scripts.//generate:capability-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-06. Joins the quality matrix, the ownership manifest, the Story DoD report, the AT index, the perf baselines and the browser-matrix ledger into packages/core/docs/capability-matrix.json, plus the narrowed projection the Storybook page imports. One row per public component, one cell per evidence row it owes, marked pass/present/stale/unrun/excepted.
scripts.//validate:capability-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-06, extended by TASK-R2-O1. Fails when the committed matrix is stale, and when a Tier D component carries an `unrun` cell with no artifact behind it -- a Tier D gap is a security gap and does not get to be an empty cell. TASK-R2-O1 adds two more hard gates over e2e/matrix/browser-evidence.json: DEGRADATION (a {component, engine, condition} cell HEAD records as `pass` may not read `unrun` or `fail` in the working tree -- `unrun` is what a lane that quietly stopped running looks like, and the message names the cell) and SHAPE (the ledger's engines and conditions must equal playwright.config.ts's, so a ledger cannot report full coverage of a lane that has grown). Stale cells and absent inputs are reported by name, never folded into a count. TASK-S1-O2 adds gate 7, the STALE RATCHET (a count plus the accepted kind set, two-way). RESIDUAL-17 adds gate 8, the EVIDENCE RATCHET on `pass` and `present`, PER KIND and TWO-WAY, closing D-RES16-3: until it existed the two numbers this repository quotes most had no baseline at all, and RESIDUAL-16 removed 42 false cells -- 27 of them published `pass` -- with all 53 links green. A rise is a loosened predicate until something shows otherwise (measured: `storyCheck` credited 27 cells for a check never asked of them) and a fall is a regression until something declares otherwise. Both are declared by ONE edit to evidenceCells.kinds in capability-matrix-ceilings.json in the same change, plus a line in its //moves log; the gate names the kind, the state, the direction and the delta and PRINTS the corrected block ready to paste, because a ratchet on `pass` must not make an honest audit expensive. It also pins the KIND SET (a new column arriving with credit already in it, or a column vanishing) and asserts totals equals the sum of kinds. No new validate:all link -- gate 8 is inside this one, so every existing link number holds.
scripts.//validate:visual-baselines: TASK-N1-O6. The authority gate for visual baselines. Every committed baseline PNG must have an entry in e2e/visual/visual-baselines.json carrying its SHA-256, the commit it was captured at, who accepted it and why. Fails on a changed digest with no recorded cause, an unaccepted (orphan) image, a recorded image that is gone, an entry with no reason/author, and a covered component missing a theme. Staleness and a gating platform that is not CI's are REPORTED. No browser: Playwright can compare a render to a baseline, it cannot tell a reviewed baseline from an overwritten one.
scripts.//validate:perf-baselines: TASK-S1-O4. The host-free half of the performance contract. Checks that packages/core/perf/baselines.json is coherent with the capture host packages/core/perf/capture-environment.json declares: every metric provenanced with a sourceCommit, no threshold derived from fewer than 5 samples or from a distribution whose cv exceeds the measurable limit, no baseline captured on a host the file does not claim, no designated gate host that none of the evidence is on, and the two one-way ratchets (metric families with no baseline; metrics recorded unmeasurable) held with the same two-way handshake the capability and visual ceilings use. It deliberately does NOT check `sourceCommit === HEAD`: a baseline file is committed by a commit whose hash did not exist when the capture ran, so that clause is satisfiable only in the seconds before the commit and false forever after. Whether THIS host may capture is a refusal inside perf:capture, not a gate -- a check that is legitimately red on every developer machine gets a --skip flag within the week.
scripts.//validate:story-dod-tiers: TASK-OSS-P5-02. The triaged half of validate:story-dod: it joins the 366 advisory items to the risk tiers and holds a per-check CEILING on the ones a tier actually requires. The ceiling only falls. A ceiling rather than zero because promoting the checks outright would land 51 red items on a green build, which this packet's own stop condition forbids. `--all` lists the open items; `--write` lowers the ceiling after a fix.
scripts.//perf:capture: TASK-OSS-P5-05. Re-measures every performance baseline: the runtime benchmarks over >= 5 separate processes (cross-process variance is where the two recorded flakes come from) and a tree-shaken fixture build per Tier C/D export. Writes packages/core/perf/baselines.json with the distribution AND the threshold it earned -- or `not yet measurable` when the spread swamps the signal. An owner action, never automatic: a suite that wrote its own baseline every run would ratchet upward forever and call it a budget. TASK-S1-O4 made that enforceable rather than advisory: an IN-PLACE write is refused unless an authoritative capture host is designated in packages/core/perf/capture-environment.json, this machine matches it, quiescence is attested with --quiet-host-attested-by <name>, and no recorded threshold would move UP (--raise-budget --owner --reason together are the only override, per doc 06). yarn perf:propose <path> is never refused.
scripts.//perf:propose: TASK-R2-O7. The same capture, written to a path you name instead of to packages/core/perf/baselines.json: `yarn perf:propose docs/.../baselines.proposed.json`. Adding a lane and replacing a budget are different acts with different authority -- a contributor measures and proposes, the owner adopts. Before this flag existed the only way to see what a new lane would record was to overwrite the file thirty-three live metrics depend on.
scripts.//perf:size-gate: D140, owner decision D135 (a), 2026-09-29. Builds the same tree-shaken one-export fixture perf:capture measured for every size:* budget in packages/core/perf/baselines.json and exits 1 naming each export over its threshold. Not behind DZUP_PERF_GATE: a gzipped byte count of a deterministic build does not vary with machine load. Blocking in the CI build job; kept out of validate:all because 22 Vite builds cost ~22 s locally and more on a CI runner. It never writes the file it reads -- raising a budget stays an owner act (perf:capture).
scripts.//validate:tokens:dtcg: TASK-N2-T1. The round-trip gate for the DTCG export: an independent DTCG reader resolves every alias and asserts each resolved value equals what dist/tokens.css computes for the same --dz-* name, in BOTH theme cascades. A name on one side and not the other fails by name. It also re-derives every ABI name from its group path (so a renamed group cannot silently rename a custom property), asserts semantic->primitive references stayed aliases instead of being inlined, checks the export's themeVarying flags against the real cascades, and holds an exact-set ceiling on cross-tier shadowing. Runs with or without a built dist/: CI runs validate:all on a clean checkout before `yarn build`, so when dist/ is absent the declaration blocks are reconstructed from the token maps and the run says so rather than passing vacuously.
scripts.//validate:tokens:refs: TASK-R5-O7. Reference integrity for the --dz-* runtime ABI, checked from the CONSUMING side: extracts every var(--dz-...) in packages/core/src/**/*.{vue,ts,css} and fails on a name nothing declares. Closes N1-O3 D4 -- 31 references once named a token the scale does not emit, 26 of them with no fallback, and five components rendered collapsed for months with every gate green. A reference WITH a fallback is a consumer hook and must be listed in token-reference-allowlist.json with its owner; a reference WITHOUT one is always a defect. Also reports the unused-token and alias-cycle ratchets from token-reference-ceilings.json. Shares the DTCG gate's CSS parser rather than growing a second one.
scripts.//validate:tokens:schema: TASK-R5-O7, closes N2-T1 D5. Validates dist/tokens.dtcg.json against the OFFICIAL DTCG 2025.10 JSON Schema, vendored at packages/tooling/src/token-checks/schemas/dtcg-format-2025.10.schema.json (spec edition in the filename). N2-T1 ran this check once, out-of-band, from a scratch script using ajv as an undeclared transitive dependency; this makes it a standing gate with no new dependency -- json-schema-draft07.ts is a minimal evaluator sized to the 20 keywords the schema uses, cross-checked against ajv in its spec. The schema is vendored rather than fetched because all 18 of its published sub-schema URLs return HTTP 404 and a gate must not touch the network. Complements validate:tokens:dtcg: schema-validity says the file is well-formed DTCG, the round-trip says it describes THIS design system.
scripts.//validate:published-imports: TASK-R1-O2 (closes N5-03 D3(2) and the Pro rehearsal's G8-7). The only gate that LOADS what it ships: packs every package in release-policy.json `published` with `yarn pack` (never `npm pack` -- that copies `workspace:*` verbatim and the tarball dies with EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL), extracts the tarballs into a scratch consumer outside the repository, and `import()`s every `exports` subpath by specifier under plain Node, plus `tsc --noEmit` on a generated probe for every `types` condition under a CONSUMER's tsconfig (no allowImportingTsExtensions, no `paths` to source). @dzup-ui/contracts shipped unloadable ESM for a whole cycle while validate:exports, validate:dts and validate:externals all passed -- each reads the built files without ever loading one, and Vite's resolver passes extensionless specifiers vacuously. Offline and script-free by construction (extraction, never `npm install`); --built turns an unbuilt or stale dist from a warning into an error.
scripts.//validate:mcp: TASK-N2-A1. Governs @dzup-ui/mcp the way a public component is governed. Fails when the generated tool surface is stale, when the version differs across package.json / server.json (x2) / CHANGELOG.md / what the server reports over MCP, when server.json's registry entry names another package or advertises an env-var default the source does not use, when a tool has no unit spec, no [malformed] case or no observed data source, or when a ratchet moves the wrong way. It does NOT import the package: packages/tooling is declared with no @dzup-ui/* dependencies, so freshness is delegated to the package's own generator in --check mode and every other clause is an independent read.
scripts.//validate:component-meta: TASK-N2-A2. The freshness gate for packages/core/docs/component-meta.json: re-extracts every component from source and fails on any byte of disagreement (sourceCommit excluded -- it is provenance, and gating on it would fail on every unrelated commit). Also fails when a public component has no record, when a description and its descriptionSource disagree, when an example carries an empty source slice, when one of the nine extraction-debt ratchets moves in either direction, and when apps/landing/scripts/build-registry.ts stops copying the artifact into /r/ -- which is the site path @dzup-ui/mcp reads in production.
scripts.//validate:provider-defaults: TASK-R5-O3, owner decisions D32(a) + D33(a). Two checks on ADR-20 s6 adoption, both measured from the GENERATED packages/core/docs/component-meta.json providerHooks, which is why this link runs straight after validate:component-meta proves that artifact fresh. (1) Every useDzDefaults consumer (provider writers excluded) must be mounted by a row of the raw-binding audit table `adoptionCases` in packages/core/src/composables/provider/provider-adoption.spec.ts, the table must be executed by describe.each, and a row naming a non-consumer is stale -- adopting the context moves each literal out of withDefaults, and 13 of the 18 components adopted in TASK-R5-O3's third session hid a reader (data-* binding, v-if, lookup map, forwarded prop) that no per-component spec asserted. On its first run it found the four earliest adopters with no row. (2) The residual -- components declaring a canonical size/tone/variant axis that do not resolve it through useDzDefaults, minus exclusions that each carry a reason and a decision -- is a downward-only ratchet in packages/tooling/src/validators/provider-defaults-ceilings.json: fails when it rises AND when it falls without the ceiling being lowered, and a stale exclusion fails. Pass --all to list the residual.
scripts.//validate:llms: TASK-N2-A3. The freshness gate for the four agent-facing markdown documents: packages/core/docs/llms{,-full}.txt (the component API) and apps/landing/public/llms{,-full}.txt (the ready-made blocks catalog -- a DIFFERENT document, deliberately, and cross-linked both ways). Fails when a committed file disagrees with a fresh render, when a fence is unbalanced or a GFM table ragged (absorbed from the orphaned apps/storybook/scripts/validate-llms.mjs, now covering four files instead of two), when a public component is not discoverable through the index and the full document by @dzup-ui/mcp's own parsing rules, when apps/storybook/scripts/build-llms.mjs stops copying the generated files into the served public/ dir, when that script starts parsing component sources again (constraint B9), when the curated intro prose states a catalog count, or when a ratchet moves in either direction. Blocks freshness is delegated to apps/landing/scripts/build-registry.ts --check-llms, which loads the catalog through Vite and compares WITHOUT writing -- packages/tooling may not depend on @dzup-ui/*. Pass --no-blocks to skip that ~20 s load.
scripts.//validate:docs-pages: TASK-N2-D1. Fails when a committed docs page disagrees with a fresh render of packages/core/docs/component-meta.json, when a public component has no page, and when a page exists that no public component produces (an orphan left by a rename). Same 'committed output vs regenerated output' shape as validate:readme-facts / validate:llms / validate:component-meta -- the generated pages are committed precisely so this comparison has something to compare against, which is TASK-N2-A3's finding F-4 applied in advance. TASK-N2-D2 widened it to apps/docs/evidence/ -- the same staleness and orphan clauses -- and added the three evidence gates described under //generate:docs-pages, so a stale or overstating evidence artifact fails here as well as in the site build.
scripts.//validate:playground-parity: TASK-N2-D3. The @vue/repl sandbox contract is stated ONCE, in packages/tooling/src/playground/playground-contract.ts: the three asset filenames the bundle producer writes, the bare specifier the sandbox import map binds, and the Tailwind browser-JIT URL without which every tv()-styled component renders unstyled. Three files restate part of it -- apps/storybook/stories/_blocks/playground.config.ts, apps/storybook/scripts/build-playground.mjs and apps/docs/scripts/sync-playground-assets.mjs -- and a drift between them is invisible to every other gate. It is not hypothetical: a third asset name (dzup-core.css) once sat in the Storybook sandbox head for a stylesheet nobody wrote, and every sandbox load 404d.
scripts.//validate:registry: TASK-R1-O5, closes A4-D3. The 282 files under apps/landing/public/r/ -- three shadcn registry indexes, 191 item payloads, 87 markdown mirrors -- were ungated. Generated is not the same as correct: this checks that every listed item has a payload beside it, that every payload is listed, that every files[] entry resolves (inline content or a real file), that no item names or imports @dzup-ui-pro (A4-F5 -- a registry COPIES source into a consumer repo and that copy is irrevocable; the Pro sources are proprietary), that the registry:theme declares both colour schemes AND aliases the dark one under dzup-ui's own [data-theme="dark"] inside @layer dz-tokens (A4-F4 -- 673+123 cssVars installed and not one selector the runtime toggles), and that no item depends on a package release-policy.json withholds. It also DECLARES the three registries, because discovery cannot see an absence: build:registry wipes public/r/ before it writes and the animations registry is written by a second script, so running one alone deletes 60 files (F-2). Run `--self-test` to watch all eight clauses fail on a seeded defect; `--all` lists the report-level findings, including the standing A4-D1 fact that every item depends on packages that 404 on npm.
scripts.//validate:docs-size: TASK-R1-O5, closes D3-F10 and half of 1.0 criterion C14. A byte ceiling on the repository's two publishable static artifacts, apps/docs/.vitepress/dist and apps/storybook/storybook-static, held in packages/tooling/src/validators/docs-size-ceilings.json. The docs site went 16.04 -> 20.67 -> 29.82 -> 33.12 MB over four packets with no budget on it at all, because check-bundle-size.mjs reads storybook-static and nothing else (D1-F-4). Down-only like every ratchet here, but measured in bytes, so each budget carries a relaxTolerance: over the ceiling fails, and so does sitting further under it than the tolerance, which is how a ceiling gets lowered instead of forgotten. An unbuilt artifact SKIPS off CI and exits 0 -- dist is a build output (ADR-12) and a fresh clone has nothing to measure, and building it inside validate:all would put a 40s VitePress build and a multi-minute Storybook build in front of every run (rejected for the same reason D149 keeps `--built` out of the chain). BUT a skip is no longer printable as a pass, and no longer honest everywhere: since 2026-09-22 (finding S6) a run with any budget skipped prints `warn docs-size: N of M measured - K SKIPPED, UNMEASURED and UNENFORCED` and never the green line, and an absent artifact is an ERROR whenever `--require-dist` is passed OR `CI` is set -- because on the machine deciding a merge, 'the artifact was never built' is a finding, not an excuse. `--allow-missing-dist` opts a pre-build CI job back out. Both budgeted artifacts are gitignored and nothing in validate:all builds them, so before this change link 38 reported green on a clean checkout having measured nothing at all. apps/docs's own build still calls it with `--require-dist`, so the enforcement point is still the build that produces the artifact.
scripts.//validate:runtime-floor: TASK-S2-O4. Can a contributor on the DECLARED floor run the mandatory gates at all? `engines.node` is `^20.19.0 || >=22.13.0` and `.nvmrc` is `20.19.0`, and two files import `globSync` from `node:fs`, which is @since v22.0.0 -- measured, not inferred: under v20.19.0 `typeof require('node:fs').globSync` is `undefined` and `vitest run packages/tooling/src/token-checks/landing-token-fallbacks.spec.ts` is exit 1 with `Tests: no tests`, against exit 0 / 9 passed under v24.14.1 on the same tree and the same node_modules. That is the 08-11 finding H4 verbatim, and it is why the validate-min-runtime CI lane cannot be green while the floor says 20. This gate does NOT fix it -- which way the contradiction resolves is open owner decision D160/D176/N5-04-D3 (register row 19) -- it stops the breach set GROWING while the decision is open. Not a duplicate of validate:engines, which asks whether the DECLARATIONS agree and whether every dependency accepts the floor: that gate is green at 4e4e46f and green while the floor is unusable, because a dependency's engines field says nothing about which built-ins this repository's own source calls. A named set with a two-way ceiling (runtime-floor-ceilings.json): a new breach fails because it is unlisted, a repaired breach fails because the entry is discharged and maxBreaches must fall in the same change, and maxBreaches must EQUAL the list so a swap cannot hide behind unchanged arithmetic. The API table is a DATA file (runtime-floor-apis.json) because the scanner matches literal substrings and a table written in the validator made the validator its own worst offender -- the first run reported 15 violations, every one a row of its own table. Fails closed on: no scanned files, an empty table, an underivable floor, a .nvmrc that disagrees with it. Chained at the END of validate:all so every existing link number holds.
scripts.//validate:browser-lane: RESIDUAL-03, closing D-S5O2-1. The wiring contract of the repository's ONLY browser-qualified lane -- apps/storybook's Vitest browser-mode project, every story's play() plus the addon-a11y axe pass in real chromium: measured 2026-09-25 at 170 files / 1,462 tests / 103.8 s. It does NOT run the lane. A gate that downloaded chromium would be switched off within the week, and a browser result is host-sensitive besides (CI is ubuntu-latest; a developer's win32 run is local evidence and qualifies nothing for anyone else). What IS repository state, needs no browser and reads identically on every host is whether the lane can still RUN and can still FAIL CI. Four silent ways it could not, three of which have happened: (1) cross-install invocation -- apps/storybook declares installConfig.hoistingLimits, so it owns its vitest/@vitest/browser/vite 6 beside the root's vite 7, and driving its config with the ROOT vitest binary (the invocation this repo's agent guidance teaches, because npx is unsafe here) launches a browser, connects it, then dies at collection with `collect 0ms` and NO error for ~7 minutes -- three agents lost ~45 minutes to it and filed a red regression that did not exist; (2) the app losing its own vitest/@vitest/browser/vite/playwright, which makes every invocation a cross-install one; (3) browser.enabled / the provider / the instance list going away, after which the suite still passes -- in jsdom -- having stopped being browser evidence with nothing saying so; (4) the CI job gaining continue-on-error or being renamed away, which is exactly the `read but cannot fail CI` state TASK-S1-O3's inputs[].gate was built to make visible. The CI clause is a TEXTUAL read of the storybook-test job block, because packages/tooling declares no runtime dependencies and a YAML parser for one job costs more than it buys. Chained at the END of validate:all so every existing link number holds.
scripts.//validate:docs-freshness: TASK-S2-O3. Is the built docs site the site THIS tree would produce? Three clauses over apps/docs/.vitepress/dist, the deployable artifact that had no binding at all: (1) `dist` -- index.html exists; absent SKIPS off CI (the dist is gitignored, ADR-12, and a fresh clone has nothing to measure) and is an ERROR under `--require-dist` or `CI`, the same policy validate:docs-size uses so two gates over one artifact do not disagree about what an absence means; (2) `stale` -- no declared input may be NEWER than the build, where the build stamp is dist/index.html's mtime (max(mtime) over all 510 files would let one touched file certify the other 509); off CI a stale build is a REPORT, because an ordinary local edit makes the dist stale within seconds and a validator that fails on that gets switched off within a week, and under `--require-dist`/CI it is an ERROR because on the machine that uploads bytes 'the artifact predates its inputs' is a finding; (3) `stamp` -- every generated artifact the site RENDERS must name the SAME sourceCommit, which is the decidable half of the evidence binding: a site whose component pages come from one commit and whose evidence pages come from another publishes a contradiction. The stamps are also PRINTED against HEAD and never failed on -- that comparison is the known-defective shape of register row #40 (an artifact is stamped with the HEAD it was generated at and goes stale the instant the owner commits). The gap it closes: validate:docs-pages compares .md against a fresh render and never opens dist; validate:docs-size measures dist's bytes and cannot tell a six-week-old build from a new one; so a pipeline could pass a ceiling, pass the page gate and publish a site describing a tree that no longer exists. Chained at the END of validate:all so every existing link number holds.
scripts.//validate:package-names: TASK-OSS-P1-01. Fails when a retired package name reappears outside the paths allowed to record history. Config is data: packages/tooling/scripts/retired-package-names.json. A file that must name a retired package -- a migration note, a test asserting it is never emitted -- says so with a `retired-name-ok: <reason>` comment on the line or the line above.
scripts.//validate:doc-snippets: TASK-OSS-P1-04. Every install snippet marked with a fixture comment must equal the fixture file a test actually builds. Documentation nothing executes drifts, and this repo has paid that bill twice: the docs advertised includePro against a package that never existed, and the module loaded a stylesheet path the tokens package does not export.
scripts.//validate:engines: TASK-OSS-P2-01 / ADR-18. The declared Node floor must (a) be the same number in package.json, .nvmrc and every CI workflow, and (b) be satisfiable by the dependencies the mandatory gates load. It was neither: engines said >=20.0.0 while vite@7 and jsdom@29 require ^20.19.0, and every CI job requested a floating major that resolves to the newest 20.x -- so the floor was a claim nothing ran on.
scripts.//validate:adr-references: TASK-OSS-P3-01, ADR-19. Every ADR-NN cited in source or prose must resolve to a document in docs/adr/ or to an entry in packages/tooling/scripts/adr-registry.json -- a ratcheted debt ledger of the 14 decisions this repository cites but has never written down. The set may only shrink. Put `adr-example-ok:` on a line to exempt an id that is an example rather than a citation.
scripts.//validate:adr-status: TASK-S0-O3, 2026-09-24. Fails when an ADR whose OWN `Status:` line says `Proposed` is cited from SHIPPED SOURCE (a non-Markdown, non-spec file under packages/<pkg>/src/), unless a dated entry in packages/tooling/src/validators/adr-status-grandfather.json covers it. Not a second copy of `maxProposedCitedFromCode`: that ceiling is a NUMBER, so accepting one ADR while a new unsigned decision becomes load-bearing leaves the arithmetic unmoved and silently green; this list is a set of NAMES, and an unlisted `Proposed` ADR fails whatever the arithmetic says (proven by seeded fixture in adr-status.spec.ts). It FAILS CLOSED: an empty scan, a missing `Status:` line or a status word outside the lifecycle vocabulary is a red with a named reason, never a pass. The list empties itself -- the day an owner flips a `Status:` line the gate goes red until the entry is deleted and maxGrandfathered lowered in the same change.
scripts.//validate:release-policy: TASK-N5-01. The gate nothing in this repository had: it RUNS `changeset status`. TASK-SK-1 found that command failing outright on `main` -- a changeset naming the ignored `@dzup-ui/tooling` alongside two published packages blocked the entire release plan -- and it had gone unseen because `validate:changelog` reads CHANGELOG.md files and no gate assembled the plan. SK-1 fixed the changeset and did not add the gate. This adds it, plus the invariants `changeset status` cannot see: every workspace package classified published/withheld/private in release-policy.json and agreeing with its own `private` flag and the changesets `ignore` array (apps/docs was created by N2-D1 and the config never heard of it); `privatePackages.version: false` so a private app cannot enter the plan (`@dzup-ui/landing` was standing in it); no changeset declaring `major` while the target is 0.x, which under packages/contracts/VERSIONING.md would ship 1.0.0 as a side effect; no pre-mode residue; and a ratchet on the count of published packages whose CHANGELOG heading `validate:changelog` would reject -- the shape `changeset version` writes.
scripts.//validate:peers: TASK-R1-O6 joined a second assertion to this link. The first half (peer-ranges.ts) checks that every declared peerDependency resolves inside its range. The second half (peer-icon-duplicates.ts) checks something no gate in this repository could see: that the icon library resolves ONCE. packages/core declares lucide-vue-next ^0.477.0 and apps/landing + apps/sandbox declare ^0.475.0; a caret on a 0.x pins the minor, so the ranges can never unify and yarn.lock carries both (N5-04-F4, measured 2026-09-03, still true at 527dbd1). validate:peers read peerDependencies only and validate:externals checks that what dist imports is DECLARED, not that it resolves once. The gate counts across an identity SET -- `lucide-vue-next` and `@lucide/vue` are the same library under two names -- because a half-finished swap leaves one version of each and a naive per-package count calls that clean. It is RED today, deliberately: the duplication is real and decision D174 (docs/program-2026-09-04/reports/peer-hygiene-decisions-2026-09.md) is what clears it.
scripts.//validate:icon-duplicates: TASK-R1-O6. The icon-library duplication gate, also reachable on its own. Reads yarn.lock (what a consumer's CI installs from) rather than node_modules (which may be absent, pruned, or pinned to a floor by test:min-peer), and cross-checks against node_modules when it exists. Four hard clauses -- single-version, single-ident, declared-family, lockfile-coverage -- plus two report-level lines for upstream deprecation and lock-vs-disk disagreement. Run `--self-test` to watch each clause fire on its own seeded defect and a clean control pass; `--json` for the machine-readable report.

scripts.//validate:all:build: RESIDUAL-01, closing D-S2O1-1 (= D-S0O1-1 option c). `yarn build` is the LAST link, appended never inserted: every link number in this repository's reports is a position in this string, the count has moved six times in a week, and inserting would silently renumber every citation. Why it exists: the build was red from 589be13 until 2026-09-23 and not one of the 59 links noticed, because a broken build is not a broken typecheck -- it is a rootDir/emit contradiction that only an emitting compiler can see.
scripts.//validate:evidence-binding: TASK-S0-O1. Proves that every generated authority artifact still describes the tree it was generated from, and does it with a question an agent CAN answer. The obvious spelling -- sourceCommit === HEAD -- has been written four times and was unsatisfiable every time: an artifact is written at HEAD = X and the commit that lands it is X+1, so a committed artifact ALWAYS stamps its own parent (see headCommit() in packages/tooling/src/quality/git.ts, which routes the off-by-one to the owner as D1). That check is therefore red on exactly the commit where the artifact is most correct -- 4e4e46f, titled "regenerate evidence at 589be13", is the proof. This one asks ORDERING instead: did any path the artifact declares itself generatedFrom change AFTER the artifact was stamped? Four rules -- the stamp is an ancestor of HEAD; no commit in (stamp, HEAD] touched a declared input; a governed artifact built from another is stamped no earlier than it; and an uncommitted input edit prints as an advisory, not a failure. The generatedFrom globs are handed to git log -- :(glob)<pattern> unchanged, so git does the matching and this repository grows no second glob implementation. Config is data: packages/tooling/src/validators/evidence-binding.json.
scripts.//qualify:package: TASK-S2-O1 — the twelve rows of 08-11 doc 08 package-qualification matrix, each against a yarn-packed tarball in a temp consumer workspace. Writes docs/qa/release/<candidate>/package-qualification.{md,json}. Exit 1 on a red row; a BLOCKED row (no second-tier tarball) does not fail the lane.
scripts.//validate:deprecations: TASK-S2-O2. The gate packages/contracts/VERSIONING.md §4 says did not exist -- it states in its own words that 'There is no repository-wide ledger of deprecated symbols' and that 'Nothing records a deprecated *prop*, *part* or *state*'. packages/contracts/deprecations.json is that ledger; this is the gate that keeps it honest in BOTH directions. Four failure modes: a symbol annotated `@deprecated` with no record (the ratchet -- 16 measured, 0 remaining); a record whose annotation is gone; an `earliestRemoval` that has passed while the symbol is still annotated; and a codemod id with no transform behind it. Plus the doc-06 schema: a named replacement, written migration instructions wherever `codemod` is null, and a REASON wherever the dev-mode runtime warning is absent or not-applicable (doc 06 says 'when practical', so an absence is conformant and an UNEXPLAINED absence is not). Prose that merely names the tag is separated by the JSDoc grammar -- code spans stripped, then the tag must OPEN its line -- not by an allowlist; the first draft without that rule reported four annotations that do not exist, all four in its own source.
scripts.//validate:stop-conditions: TASK-S2-O2. The eleven 08-11 doc 08 release stop conditions as an executable gate -- they existed only as prose, and nothing refused a release when a threshold had been raised or evidence was bound to another commit. doc 08 prints NINE bullets; its first is compound ('dirty/unidentified source, generated drift, or evidence bound to a different commit/configuration') and names three failures with three remedies, so the enumeration is 3 + 8 = ELEVEN. It FAILS CLOSED: `fired` (the condition is met), `unevaluable` (it could not be decided, with the command that would make it decidable) and `unattested` (awaiting an owner signature) are all RED; only `clear` is green. Ten are machine-checked; SC-11 (authority) is attested, because a repository can see that an action did not happen but never whether one that did was authorised -- an agent may never sign it. Two conditions became mechanically detectable only at 4e4e46f, when TASK-S2-O1 built the twelve-row qualification matrix: fail-open (rows 8/9) and tarball-differs (row 11). NOT in validate:all -- it fires SC-1 on any dirty worktree, which is correct for a release and useless for a per-change gate; it belongs to rehearse:release. Flags: --candidate, --only (a diagnostic, NOT a release verdict), --json, --write-ratchets (records this candidate's ceilings so the NEXT candidate's SC-7 has a baseline).
scripts.//generate:release-report: TASK-S2-O2. `release:report` with the eight-section invariant ENFORCED rather than intended: --verify-sections exits 1 unless the rendered document carries exactly the eight sections 08-11 doc 08 section Required release report names, in order. A section with no evidence prints the absence in words; it is never dropped, because dropping one collapses two rungs of the maturity ladder. Extends the TASK-R1-O3 generator rather than replacing it -- section 5 now also projects TASK-S2-O1's twelve-row package-qualification matrix, and section 8 now carries the eleven stop conditions, the attested rows the owner must sign, and the deprecation ledger's with/without-record counts.
scripts.//report:peer-surface: TASK-N5-04. Which external packages each PUBLISHED entry point of @dzup-ui/core can reach, plus the lucide-vue-next glyph inventory -- both read from dist/, because an exports map and a barrel's re-export shape are properties of the artifact, not of src/. The distinction it exists to make measurable: `reka-ui` is a package-level peer, but DzButton.vue.js reaches five externals and reka-ui is not one of them, while the ./buttons barrel -- the only published way to import DzButton -- reaches it through DzSpeedDial -> DzTooltip. A REPORT, not a gate: exit 0 always, no baseline, no ratchet, deliberately outside validate:all, because every number depends on decisions the owner has not taken (peer-hygiene-2026-09.md). Run after a build.
scripts.//test:perf: TASK-OSS-P5-05 + TASK-R2-O7. Both halves of the perf harness: the runtime/size benchmarks (perf-bench.spec.ts, in the root config) and the four lanes doc 06 asks for -- leak, long task, memory, hydration (perf-lanes/, in a config of their own so 1,100 mounts of the catalogue's heaviest components stay out of `yarn test`). Every metric REPORTS always and FAILS only under DZUP_PERF_GATE=1; the lanes' seeded-failure checks are unconditional, so a broken detector is loud with the gate off.
scripts.//test:nuxt-fixtures: TASK-OSS-P1-03. Real Nuxt consumer apps, installed from packed tarballs and staged OUTSIDE this repository -- a fixture kept inside the monorepo resolves the repo's own nuxt/nitropack/vite through Node's upward directory walk and stops being a consumer test. Three steps because one install is ~800 packages and one build is ~60s: :pack (yarn pack + stage), :install (npm install each), then the assertions. Set DZUP_PRO_TARBALL to a tarball produced by a Pro checkout to include the core-pro fixture; without it that fixture reports `unrun`, not `skipped`.
scripts.//test:vue-next: TASK-N5-03. ADVISORY forward-compatibility lane: the unit + contract suite against the Vue 3.6 release candidate, including the Vapor-interop smoke (packages/core/tests/vapor-interop.spec.ts, which reports `unverified` rather than passing on the default Vue). It applies `resolutions` to package.json, installs, runs, then restores BOTH package.json and yarn.lock and VERIFIES the restore -- exit 3 if the tree is left dirty, which it treats as worse than a failing suite. Exit 2, not 1, when the install itself fails: 'never executed here' and 'this is broken' are not interchangeable. A red run is a fact about an unreleased Vue, not a defect claim against this repository, and it does not gate a merge until `vue@latest` is 3.6.x -- that trigger is in docs/program-2026-09/reports/N5-03-toolchain-migration-memo.md. NOT wired into validate:all or `yarn test` on purpose. `node_modules` still holds the lane's Vue afterwards; `yarn install` puts it back.
scripts.//test:min-peer: TASK-R1-O4. The MINIMUM declared peer lane: `@dzup-ui/core` publishes `vue: ^3.5.0` and `reka-ui: ^2.0.0`, and nothing had ever installed either floor -- the root manifest depends on `vue@^3.5.13` and the tree resolves `reka-ui@2.9.x`, so every lane in this repository has only ever measured the newest version the lockfile admits. It derives each floor FROM `peerDependencies` at run time (never a literal here, which would be a second declaration that drifts), pins it with `resolutions`, installs, ASSERTS the version on disk equals the floor, runs typecheck + the core/contracts/nuxt suites, then restores BOTH package.json and yarn.lock and verifies the restore. Exit 2 -- not a warning and not a pass -- when the floor does not land on disk: a lockfile can silently lift a floor, and a green run about the wrong version is worse than no run. UNLIKE test:vue-next this is NOT advisory: 3.5.0 and 2.0.0 are released versions this repository tells consumers to expect, so a red run is a defect claim against this repository. NOT wired into validate:all or `yarn test` -- it needs its own full install. `node_modules` holds the floor versions afterwards; `yarn install` puts the default toolchain back.

scripts.//visual:accept: TASK-N1-O6. Accept exactly ONE visual baseline, with --by and --reason both required: `yarn visual:accept --component DzButton --theme dark --by "<name>" --reason "<what changed and why the new image is correct>"`. One snapshot per invocation is the constraint that replaces the perf lane's downward ratchet -- a different image is not `worse`, so the cost of accepting scales with how much changed instead. --record-only re-digests an image already on disk; --bootstrap records baselines that have no entry yet and can never re-accept a changed one.

scripts.//docs:verify: TASK-S2-O3. The CI-agnostic lane a deploy pipeline calls BEFORE it uploads a byte. The 2026-09-04 docs-deployment packet described an eight-step docs-deploy job and correctly refused to write it (writing a workflow that deploys is an owner act); the cost was that its gates stayed a list in a report. This is that list, executable, with no host, no credential and no upload in it -- so the pipeline configuration reduces to: checkout, install, `yarn docs:verify`, upload apps/docs/.vitepress/dist. Five checks, none re-implemented here: (1) build = `docs:build` (a stale component-meta.json turns it red via its own generate step, a DEAD INTERNAL LINK turns it red because .vitepress/config.ts does not ignore them, and it ends in validate:docs-size --require-dist); (2) size = validate:docs-size --require-dist --all (measured bytes vs the DECLARED budget, both printed, plus the ten largest files); (3) registry = validate:registry --all (the 191 items resolve, plus the resolution ledger: how many a consumer could actually install); (4) links = check:links -- external only, NO second link checker was added because internal links are the build's job; (5) freshness = validate:docs-freshness --require-dist + validate:docs-pages + validate:playground-parity. Flags: `--skip-build` reuses the dist (step 5 still catches a stale one), `--require-installable` makes registry tier 3 fail closed and is what the deploy lane passes, `--offline` drops the external link check. Every step's own exit code is printed, because 'docs:verify failed' is not actionable and 'step 3 registry exited 1' is. It deploys NOTHING: see docs/program-2026-09-22-architecture/reports/TASK-S2-O3-deploy-runbook.md.

NOT `changeset publish`: under Yarn it runs `npm publish`, which ships `workspace:*` ranges verbatim, and it publishes every non-private package including the withheld compat/codemods. `release:publish` publishes release-policy.json's `published` list through `yarn npm publish`; `changeset tag` then prints the `New tag:` lines the action turns into pushed tags and GitHub releases. `--provenance` needs GitHub Actions OIDC, so this script is CI-only.

scripts.//release:api-surface:record: TASK-R1-O3. Records the public API surface of every `published` package, read through the TypeScript compiler from the PACKED declarations, into packages/tooling/api-surface/<sha>.json -- the baseline the NEXT release is diffed against. REFUSES on a dirty tree: a baseline taken from a tree nobody can check out is a number with no referent, and the next release would report changes against content that exists in no commit (08-11 doc 08's first release stop condition). `--force` records an INADMISSIBLE snapshot, stamped `admissible: false`, for exercising the machinery only. Running this once on a clean commit is the only thing that moves `release:api-diff` out of its degraded manifest-only mode.
scripts.//release:api-diff: TASK-R1-O3. Diffs the packed public surface against a baseline, classifies every change against packages/contracts/VERSIONING.md and maps it to the changeset level the 0.x policy REQUIRES -- breaking = `minor`, additive = `patch`, `major` refused. Pro's api-diff maps breaking to `major`; porting that verbatim would emit a changeset every gate here refuses. Three fidelities, and every run says which it used: `snapshot` (full -- names, kinds, props, emits, slots, signatures), `manifest-only` (names only; renames indistinguishable from removal+addition, reported rather than guessed) and `none` (no baseline at all -- symbols reported as unbaselined, never as `added`). Every run ALSO reconciles the packed surface against public-api.manifest.json, which is the `generate:exports` drift measured instead of quoted: a symbol the barrel exports that the manifest does not list is one the next `yarn generate:exports` DELETES. Writes docs/qa/release/<bundle>/api-diff.{json,md}. Reports stop conditions; blocks nothing.
scripts.//release:evidence: TASK-R1-O3. The supply-chain half of 08-11 doc 08 section Package ('SBOM, vulnerability/license report, provenance/hash', required per release): a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM per tarball plus an aggregate, a vulnerability report keyed by EXACT resolved version against the endpoint `npm audit` uses, a licence report classified with the SAME allow/block sets `validate:licenses` gates on (one policy, not two) with owned exceptions in packages/tooling/scripts/licence-exceptions.json, sha256+sha512 per tarball AND per file inside it, and an unsigned in-toto/SLSA provenance statement that records in its own body that trusted publishing has never been exercised. A query that could not run is `status: not-run` with a reason, NEVER a zero. Publishes, signs, installs and mutates nothing.
scripts.//release:report: TASK-R1-O3. Renders docs/qa/release/<bundle>/report.md with the EIGHT sections 08-11 doc 08 section Required release report names, plus ledger.md (the gate-by-gate row ledger) and candidate-content-digest.json. It is a PROJECTION: every row comes from a companion artifact in the bundle (api-diff.json, supply-chain.json, hashes.json, results.jsonl) or from a generated artifact in the repository, quoted with the commit it stamps. Nothing is typed by hand and no row is promoted because a file exists (Pro evidence-layer finding E-4). With no results.jsonl, sections 2 and 3 report UNRUN rather than green.
scripts.release:bundle: yarn release:api-diff && yarn release:evidence && yarn release:report
